text:
Maria Ramos: Quick question — when routing requests from hosted -> private sidecar, what headers/tokens do we guarantee to propagate? Specifically: tenant-id, forwarded-org, x-request-id. Private on-prem sidecars use customer HSM/cert chains, so can we rely on Redwood KMS tokens to be present?

Jon Patel: We currently propagate tenant-id and x-request-id. We DO NOT forward internal service tokens. For private deployments we use an attestation flow: sidecar mTLS + a signed attestation header. See stub:

```
X-Tenant-ID: <tenant>
X-Request-ID: <uuid>
X-Attest: signed::<base64>
```

Alice Chen: Edge-case: if the Private sidecar is unhealthy and we fallback to Dedicated, we must not leak the customer's HSM session cert. Proposed behavior: strip customer cert, mint a redwood ephemeral with scoping (read-only, no key-export), add header `X-Route-Origin: private-failover`, and write an audit-event. Thoughts?

Kevin O'Neill: Agree with the ephemeral mint. Also add `route_origin` tag in telemetry and persist an `audit_id` that links the failover trace. Circuit-breaker probe to sidecar should be quick (50ms) and we should give up after 2 failed probes before flipping to Dedicated. Example probe curl:

`curl -k --cert <sidecar-cert> https://sidecar/healthz -H "X-Tenant-ID: 123"`

Maria Ramos: Can someone file a tiny RFC/checklist? I'll draft the telemetry changes. Need these items: header mapping docs, attestation format, failover header semantics, kms_mode tag, audit event schema.

deploy-bot: scheduled deploy to staging: service-routing v0.92 — routing feature flags and probe changes rolled out

Alice Chen: ack :thumbsup:

Jon Patel: I'll PR the attestation schema and a small test matrix for hosted->private->dedicated paths. Will include examples for SDK behavior on 401 vs 502.

Maria Ramos: thanks everyone — will sync next Tuesday 10am to finalize checklist.
